summary: Feed s140_double to APM is degraded: 21.2% one-way TCP sessions and 5.6% packet loss detected. Both faults are high severity and will impair APM transaction latency and response-time calculations.

findings.root_cause: 28 of 132 TCP sessions (21.2%) show traffic in only one direction. Most likely the capture is single-sided - SPAN/TAP only mirroring Tx or Rx, or packet broker not aggregating both directions of the flow to the same tool port, or asymmetric routing with capture on only one path.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM requires both directions to correlate requests/responses and calculate latency. With 21% one-way sessions it will miss transactions, report incomplete flows, and produce inaccurate response-time metrics.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregating both directions ensures the APM sees client request and server response together for correct transaction correlation.

findings.root_cause: 96 of 1713 TCP packets (5.6%) show gaps/retransmissions indicating missing data in transit. Classic SPAN oversubscription/buffer exhaustion or packet broker congestion dropping packets under load. Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is upstream of the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: Even though APM does not require full payload, 5.6% missing packets causes incomplete flow records, false retransmission/loss alarms, and skewed latency calculations, reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Passive TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy unlike SPAN which drops when oversubscribed or buffers fill, eliminating the 5.6% gaps.
